title: Decay of separated subharmonic level components
exact_target: How slowly can the uniformly negative contributions of disjoint subharmonic level components decay?
definition_tex:
\subsection{Definitions and mathematical statement}
Let $A=\{z:1<|z|<2\}$ and let $u$ be subharmonic
there, not identically $-\infty$. Suppose that
$D_1,D_2,\ldots$ are pairwise disjoint open subsets of $A$,
each a union of connected components of $\{u<0\}$.
For each $k$, choose a number $\delta_k>0$ such that
for every radius $r\in(1,2)$,
\[
 \int_{\{\theta\in[0,2\pi):\,re^{i\theta}\in D_k\}}
                      u(re^{i\theta})\,d\theta
                         \leq-\delta_k.
\]
Thus each group of negative components contributes a fixed
positive amount of negative angular integral on every circle
of the annulus. The lower amount may depend on $k$, but
not on $r$.

Determine the possible decay of the positive sequence
$(\delta_k)$ under these hypotheses. The substantive issue
is sharp necessary restrictions and matching constructions,
up to reordering the components and multiplying $u$ and
all $\delta_k$ by a common positive constant.
In particular, determine the sharp summability consequences:
for which exponents $p>0$ must every admissible sequence
satisfy $\sum_k\delta_k^p<\infty$, and what occurs at the
limiting exponent?

The source gives exponentially decaying examples and a
universal power-summability restriction, leaving a gap
between realizations and upper restrictions. The target is
to close that gap for general subharmonic functions.
No harmonicity, finite number of components, or radial
symmetry assumption is imposed.

\subsection{Short English statement}
How slowly can the uniformly negative contributions of disjoint subharmonic level components decay?
